title: AI trading bots vs AI Trading Agents: what’s the actual difference?
author: OwlZealousideal4779
selftext:
I have been looking into the AI trading tools. I am wondering how people here actually see the difference between an AI trading bot and a real Trading Agent.  
  
I am currently working with Alphio AI which is focused on AI-powered trading AI crypto trading and Trading Agents and one thing I have noticed is that the term AI trading bot seems to cover a lot of tools.  
  
Some systems just follow set rules or indicators while others say they use AI to look at market conditions and change how they work.  
  
So where do people here think the line is?  
  
Does a real AI Trading Agent have to do more than make signals or follow set strategies? For example should it be able to look at kinds of market information think through changes and change how it works over time?  
  
For people who have used AI trading bots or AI crypto trading bots what features really made a difference?  
  
I would like to hear what people here think is truly helpful, versus another product using AI as a way to sell something.

comments.author: do0fusz
comments.body: A bot is told what to do, an agent is told what the desired end result is.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: The real difference is that a bot follows pre-set rules or indicators, while an agent interprets market conditions, adapts its strategy over time, and can act on broader goals rather than just executing signals.

replies.author: ditchtheworkweek
replies.body: How do you backtest an agent?

replies.author: tradematesHQ
replies.body:
Backtesting an agent is tricky because its decisions change based on market context, not fixed rules. You’d need to simulate a range of market regimes and let the agent adapt within each run, then compare outcomes across many iterations to see if its learning actually improves results over a static bot.

At trademates.co we Backtest with our in-house ML engine where the ai learns from each single analysis and improves its own cubic algorithm.
